clue.text: Leave one in storage compartment a year

indicators.note: the word in tells us the numeral one is placed within the storage space

parts.note: a ship's hold is its cargo compartment
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone stashes things in a locker for a year before taking leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave from work, as in annual leave, is time off, a synonym.

clue.text: Get engaged in gameshow

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the single word gameshow

explanation.surface: A couple get engaged on a television quiz programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears mesh when their teeth interlock, so to engage with each other is the mechanical sense.

clue.text: Subordinate as slave endlessly mistreated

indicators.note: mistreated letters are knocked about into a new order
endlessly means the final letter of slave is dropped

explanation.surface: A subordinate, as a slave, suffers constant abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims slave to SLAV; 'mistreated' then rearranges AS + SLAV.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal vassal was a subordinate holding land from a lord in return for service.

clue.text: Official person showin' courage

parts.note: a man is a person
daring means showing courage; the dropped g matches the apostrophe in showin'

explanation.surface: A bureaucrat speaks informally about a brave individual.
explanation.walkthrough: The clipped 'showin'' tells you the synonym also drops its final G: DARIN'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin was a high official of imperial China, and now any senior civil servant.

clue.text: Drunk is paid to go round Arab country drinking too much

indicators.note: to go round means the scrambled letters encircle the country
drunk suggests the letters of is paid are reeling into a new order

parts.note: Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A tipsy traveller is paid to tour a Gulf state while boozing heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' rearranges IS PAID into DIPSIA, which 'to go round' wraps about OMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipsomania is a morbid craving for alcohol, the habit of excessive drinking.

clue.text: Property set fire to in harbour

indicators.note: in places the burning word within the harbour word

parts.note: a quay is a landing place in a harbour
lit is the past tense of light, to set fire to

explanation.surface: An arsonist torches a building on the waterfront.
explanation.definitionFit: A quality is an attribute or characteristic, the same sense as a property of a substance.

clue.text: Bars impressionist following personal problem

indicators.note: following places the painter after the personal problem

parts.note: BO is body odour, a classic personal problem
Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: Pubs feature an impersonator coming on after someone with a hygiene issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressionist' suggests a comic mimic, but it is the painter Degas.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodegas are Spanish wine bars or shops, so bars in the drinking sense.

clue.text: Shakespearean prince, I save swimmer

parts.note: Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays
save and but both mean except

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's prince declares he will rescue a drowning bather.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish is a swimmer in crossword usage, and this is a large flatfish.

clue.text: Music-maker such as ear drum put first

indicators.note: put first tells us the drum word comes before the ear word

parts.note: a drum is a cylindrical container, a barrel
an ear is an example of an organ of the body

explanation.surface: A musician ranks the drum ahead of anything played by ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A street instrument cranked by hand, it produces tunes from a pinned cylinder.

clue.text: Fling one off bedside table

indicators.note: off means the word one is taken away from the fling phrase

parts.note: a one-night stand is a brief fling

explanation.surface: Someone hurls a piece of furniture beside the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fling' looks like a verb (throw), but it is a brief affair: a one-night stand, minus ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightstand is a small piece of furniture placed next to a bed, especially in American usage.

clue.text: Sailor's pungent wit

definitions.meaning: a veteran seaman; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A seaman is known for his sharp humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a seasoned seaman and sharp, piquant wit go by this one word.

clue.text: Rebel having certain amount of power overturned bank

parts.note: a watt is a unit of power

indicators.note: overturned in a down sense means the word for bank is read backwards

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on

explanation.surface: A rebel with some clout capsized a financial institution.
explanation.walkthrough: Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381.
explanation.definitionFit: He led an uprising against the poll tax, the archetypal English rebel.

clue.text: Inarticulate guide to net needs rewriting

indicators.note: needs rewriting says these letters must be written out again in another order

explanation.surface: A clumsy manual on netting fish must be redrafted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to speak fluently from shyness or emotion is struggling for words.

clue.text: Sends second clock back

indicators.note: back means the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a timer is a clock for measuring time

explanation.surface: Someone puts the clock back a second.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to send money or refer a matter elsewhere, so it means dispatches.

clue.text: Minion touring Northern Ireland showing stress

indicators.note: touring means the minion goes all around Northern Ireland

parts.note: a minion is an underling, a subordinate

explanation.surface: A lackey travelling round Ulster looks frazzled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing stress' suggests strain; it means emphasising text.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing a line beneath words is a way of emphasising them, so emphasising is the sense.

clue.text: What Americans did to get Reagan in charge

parts.note: American voters elected Reagan as president
Ronald Reagan, known as Ron

explanation.surface: US voters put Ronald Reagan in power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in charge' looks like a phrase about power; 'charge' alone is the definition, a particle carrying electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The fundamental particle carries one unit of negative electric charge, by extension standing for it.

clue.text: Saving company invested in money supply

indicators.note: invested in puts the company inside the reworked money
supply read as supple-y, loosely, so these letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: A firm putting money into its cash flow is thrifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is an unusual anagram signal, read as the adverb from supple (pliantly); it gives ENOMY, which 'invested in' opens after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Economy means careful management of resources, avoiding waste, which is thrift.

clue.text: Knocking down patio feature?

definitions.meaning: to deck someone is to floor them with a punch
wooden boarding laid as a garden floor; the query marks a loose definition

explanation.surface: Demolishing part of a garden terrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the punching sense and timber garden flooring share the same spelling.

clue.text: Expert having caught American in charge

indicators.note: in puts the caught letter and American inside the expert

parts.note: an ace is an expert
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
US is the United States, so American

explanation.surface: A specialist who caught a Yank is now in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in charge' looks like one phrase, but 'in' is the insertion and 'charge' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone formally with an offence is to indict or blame them.

clue.text: Engineers safe capturing advanced weapon

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: capturing means the safe word holds the advanced letter

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: Army sappers seize a strongbox and a high-tech gun.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER is old underworld slang for a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeater is a firearm that fires several shots without reloading.

clue.text: Old copper item found in kitchen

definitions.meaning: early policemen were named after Sir Robert Peel
a gadget for paring potatoes and fruit

explanation.surface: An antique copper pan sits in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like the metal; it is slang for a police officer. Peel founded London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the Victorian policeman and the paring utensil take this name.

clue.text: Flier in difficulty

definitions.meaning: a small sandpiper, a wading bird
a tangled problem, as a knotty one

explanation.surface: A pilot is in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the wading bird and an entangled problem share the name.

clue.text: Characteristics of what banks in Munich used to do?

definitions.text: what banks in Munich used to do?
definitions.meaning: before the euro, German banks dealt in Deutschmarks

explanation.surface: Traits of old Bavarian banking practice.
explanation.walkthrough: Germany used the Deutschmark until the euro arrived in 2002.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's distinctive habits are figuratively their signature traits or hallmarks.

clue.text: Car valuation regularly disregarded

indicators.note: regularly disregarded drops every other letter of valuation, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: A vehicle's price estimate is routinely ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Auto is a short, chiefly American word for an automobile.

clue.text: Caesar rejected traveller in his city

indicators.note: rejected means the whole assembly is turned back to front
in places the traveller inside the city

parts.note: Caesar's city is Rome
a rep is a travelling sales representative

explanation.surface: Julius Caesar spurned a visitor to Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his city' leans on the surface: Caesar's city is Rome. 'rejected' turns the combined ROREPME round.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman emperors bore the title Caesar, and the word became a byword for an imperial ruler.

clue.text: Fate of French mistress's last minute

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word mistress's

parts.note: minute, pronounced my-NEWT, means tiny

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman's lover's final moment seals his fate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' looks like a unit of time; it is the adjective meaning very small.
explanation.definitionFit: Destiny is the predetermined course of events, a synonym of fate.
